lines.watchItem: The four largest cloud buyers have lifted planned 2026 spending to roughly $725 billion, up 77% on last year, and new entrants such as SpaceX are now spending billions a quarter on AI compute. That pull sits upstream of every advanced-node and packaging order book.

Advanced packaging is booked out through 2027 with lead times of 52 to 78 weeks even as capacity climbs toward 125,000-130,000 wafers a month, yet memory is now the tighter limit: Nvidia is cutting memory per accelerator to stretch a fixed high-bandwidth memory pool. The exposure is that added packaging capacity converts into fewer shipped systems than the order book implies.

MediaTek has raised its AI accelerator share target to 15-20% from 10-15% and sizes the 2027 accelerator market at $80 billion excluding memory. Custom accelerator programs are becoming a second concentration of packaging demand alongside the incumbent GPU vendor, and their route choices move the same scarce capacity.

Margins are wide at every step of the chain right now: 67.7% at the foundry, 75% at the chip vendor, and memory makers holding pricing power as next-generation memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027. Watch whether memory pricing quietly absorbs margin that currently sits with the foundry step.

Intel's rival packaging line is reported above 90% yield, aimed at 2027 volume at roughly half the cost of the incumbent approach, while Intel Foundry revenue grew 31% year on year to $5.8 billion on better yields. An alternative packaging route at half the price is the clearest medium-term threat to the current packaging position.

A growing slice of the demand is financed by the seller or by debt: the chip vendor has discussed a $350 billion facility backing one customer's purchases and backstopped its data-center debt, while Alphabet funded its build with $49.6 billion of equity and $20.3 billion of notes and posted its first negative free cash flow. Orders resting on vendor and debt financing are the ones most likely to move if credit conditions turn.
